authority.note: This proof compares stress evidence/review resolution only; it cannot rank decks or decide swaps.

before.limitation: Every deck received the same generic scenario set; opponent-facing stack/stax and bracket-specific adversarial questions were not assigned as distinct workloads.

conclusion: Step F resolves the prior one-size-fits-all stress layer into distinct B5/B4 workloads, exact evidence routing, executed bounded mechanic evidence and mandatory adversarial review prompts without producing a composite stress score.
limitations: This is a before/after evidence-resolution comparison, not benchmark accuracy or deck power measurement.
Existing M3 outcomes are reused under their original preregistration; Step F does not retroactively change thresholds.
Step-E deck-level module execution is bounded availability/friction evidence from the frozen development snapshot, not multiplayer outcome simulation.
Red-team prompts remain pending judgment and are not counted as passed/failed stresses.
Priority weights are workload allocation only and never outcome weights.

real_deck_examples.resolution_gain: Generic M3 scenarios are now placed in a bracket-specific workload together with executed bounded Step-E canonical-deck evidence and mandatory adversarial prompts; no outcome is aggregated.
